# Read ownership versus write admission

These are synthetic serialized contracts generated by `generate.py`, not Blender-certified scenes or production templates.

- `unknown-id.blend`: the first Object-shaped header has an unknown two-byte ID code. Contextual getters retain its DATA scope; Dependency tracing does not enumerate it as an Object. Strict graph admission refuses it.
- `data-before-id.blend`, `data-after-control.blend`: unreferenced top-level DATA is ignored by native readfile, rather than refusing the entire read. Strict FILE-OPS admission still refuses the malformed publication layout.
- `raw-linked-id.blend`: a bare linked ID uses schema index zero (ID in this deliberately small SDNA). Its ID-valued hops still select the linked placeholder and global Library. No write qualification is implied.
- `data-after-placeholder.blend`: linked placeholder reading returns before the DATA-map read; following DATA is ignored by the top-level reader, not assigned to the placeholder.

`src/owner_compat_tests.rs` tests actual trace/getter entries, source import admission and census/write refusal. The source-derived table test constructs Palette, ParticleSettings, Speaker and Collection records in the pinned native SDNA and asserts the legacy Group/Screen/Lamp aliases; that is a typed-layout proof, not fresh native receiving.
